title: Strict extraction with the prescribed ordinary evaluations
statement: Let J be an essentially small site in a chosen coefficient universe and let B_n be commutative ring sheaves with adjacent maps τ_n : B_(n+1) → B_n [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Define a functor from Systems J B τ to StrictRingSystem (rings J B τ) [def-pur-system-level-left-extension-basic] by taking its level n to be exactly (evaluation J B τ n).obj M and its transition for n≤m to be exactly (transition J B τ h).app M. On a system morphism f its level n is exactly (evaluation J B τ n).map f. The identity and composition laws are the sectionwise laws of the source presheaf. No epimorphism or normalization condition is imposed on transitions. These literal choices avoid applying arbitrary coefficient inverse images to an additional change-of-coefficient identification.

source.place: Construction 4.1, printed p. 21: module systems, their evaluations, and horizontal restriction maps; the generic site model is def-coef-semilinear-system-models.

proof.text: Use the already constructed evaluation module sheaves as the levels and the already constructed semilinear horizontal maps as transitions. The defining section formula of transition identifies its underlying function with the original source-presheaf horizontal restriction. For an identity index, the horizontal arrow is the identity of the product category, so the presheaf identity law proves the required section equation. For l≤m≤n, the horizontal arrow for l≤n is the composite of the other two horizontal arrows, so the presheaf composition law gives exactly the required strict composition equation.

proof.text: A morphism is sent to its evaluation at each index. The naturality square of the existing transition transformation is precisely the required strict-system morphism square. Evaluation preserves identities and compositions, and strict-system morphism extensionality checks these laws componentwise. This is the explicit sourceStrictFunctor construction, with all auxiliary laws proved.
